blind_spots.blind_spot: Kubernetes-microservice orchestration assumes cloud-ops talent at the deployment site
blind_spots.operator_reality: A tactical enclave running Spacetime has no SRE on the watch floor; a crashed pod in an air-gapped enclave stays crashed until someone cleared and trained shows up
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Alphabet heritage — the team's baseline is Google-grade infrastructure operated by professional SREs
blind_spots.evidence_quote: As a distributed cloud-native system of microservices, with open APIs, Spacetime is available as a managed service in Aalyria-hosted or customer-hosted Kubernetes environments.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Plug-and-play' optical terminals still need field alignment, cleaning, and sustainment
blind_spots.operator_reality: A gimballed 170mm laser terminal at a dusty austere site needs optics maintenance, spares, and a trained hand — none of which 'plug-and-play' provides; fog and particulates kill FSO links exactly when contested RF makes them most needed
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Terminal development is National-Lab rooted; demos happen with engineers on hand, not an E-5 with 20 minutes of training
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Tightbeam terminals are plug-and-play with native Spacetime integration

blind_spots.blind_spot: Federation between networks presumes other orchestrators expose cooperative APIs
blind_spots.operator_reality: Government transport rides prime-run and legacy GFE networks whose owners have no Spacetime-compatible orchestrator and no contractual reason to federate; the interconnect brokering has no counterparty in a real program
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The federation model was designed around commercial operators who want to sell transit, not DoD program offices guarding accreditation boundaries
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Open APIs allow Spacetime to federate with other network orchestrators to broker and schedule on-demand interconnect & transit across networks

opener_hook: Aalyria's Spacetime whitepaper commits to customer-hosted, air-gapped Kubernetes deployments — the R2C2 delivery order will test who on a government watch floor actually operates those microservices.
what_they_do: Alphabet-spinout (~99 people) selling Spacetime, a network-orchestration PaaS for satellites/aircraft in motion, and Tightbeam 100 Gbps laser-comms terminals to commercial and defense customers.
